text: Which of the following is a well-defined set?
options: The collection of most dangerous animals
The collection of best cricketers in the world
The collection of all natural numbers less than 100
The collection of all tall students in a class
explanation: Being less than 100 is an objective, verifiable criterion, so membership is unambiguous — the other collections depend on subjective judgement.

text: If A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, which statement is correct?
explanation: A lists the elements 1 through 6, so 5 is a member; 8, 0 and 10 are not in the list.

text: The set {x : x is an integer and −3 ≤ x < 7} in roster form has how many elements?
explanation: Integers from −3 up to but not including 7 are −3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4,5,6 — 10 elements.

text: Which of the following sets is empty?
options: {x : x is a natural number less than 1}
{x : x is a natural number, x < 5 and x > 7}
{x : x is an even prime number}
explanation: No natural number is both <5 and >7, and no natural number is less than 1 — both describe the empty set φ.

text: How many subsets does the set {1, 2, 3} have in total (including φ and the set itself)?
explanation: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets; here n = 3, so 2³ = 8.

text: If A = {a, b, c} and B = {b, c, d}, which is true?
explanation: The common elements of A and B are b and c, so A ∩ B = {b, c}; neither set is wholly contained in the other.
A ∪ B = {1,2,3,4,6,8}; its complement in U = {1..9} is {5,7,9}, the elements of U not in A ∪ B.

text: For any two sets A and B, (A ∪ B)′ equals:
explanation: This is De Morgan's law: the complement of a union is the intersection of the complements.
A − B removes from A any element also in B; only 12 is common, so the rest of A remains: {3,6,9,15,18,21}.

text: The interval (−3, 0) in set-builder form is:
explanation: Round brackets on both ends mean both endpoints are excluded — a strict open interval.

text: If set A has 3 elements and B = {3,4,5}, how many elements does A × B have?
If A = {1,2}, B = {3,4}, how many subsets (relations) can be formed from A to B?
explanation: n(A×B)=4, and the number of relations = number of subsets of A×B = 2⁴ = 16.

text: For the relation R = {(x,y): y = x+1} on A = {1,2,3,4,5,6}, what is the range?
explanation: Applying y=x+1 to each domain value 1-5 gives range values 2,3,4,5,6.

text: A function f: A → B must satisfy which condition?
options: Every element of A has at least one image in B
Every element of A has exactly one image in B
Every element of B has exactly one pre-image in A
A and B must have the same number of elements
explanation: The defining property of a function is that each domain element maps to exactly one (unique) element of the codomain.

text: If f(x) = x², what is the range of f when the domain is R (all real numbers)?
explanation: Squares of real numbers are never negative and can be arbitrarily large, so the range is all non-negative reals [0, ∞).

text: Given f(x) = 2x − 5 and g(x) = x², what is (f+g)(2)?
The domain of the real function f(x) = 1/(x−3) is:
explanation: f is undefined when the denominator is zero, i.e. at x=3, so the domain excludes 3.

text: The domain of f(x) = √(x − 1) (real-valued) is:
explanation: The expression under a square root must be non-negative for a real output, so x − 1 ≥ 0, i.e. x ≥ 1.

text: If f(x) = x³, this function is an example of:
explanation: f(−x) = (−x)³ = −x³ = −f(x), which is the defining property of an odd function.

text: The Cartesian product A × B is defined as:
explanation: By definition, the Cartesian product is the set of all ordered pairs with first coordinate from A and second from B.

explanation: 1 radian = 180/π degrees ≈ 57.2958°, i.e. about 57°16′.

text: The graph of the solution set of x > 3 on a number line is represented by:
options: A closed circle at 3, shading left
An open circle at 3, shading left
A closed circle at 3, shading right
An open circle at 3, shading right
explanation: Strict inequality (>) uses an open circle (3 itself excluded) with shading to the right (greater values).

text: For the system x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, the feasible region lies in which quadrant?
explanation: Both coordinates non-negative describes exactly the first quadrant (including the axes).

text: How many 2-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1,2,3,4,5 with no digit repeated?
explanation: Number of arrangements of 5 digits taken 2 at a time = P(5,2) = 5×4 = 20.

text: In how many ways can 6 people be seated in a row?
explanation: 6 distinct people in 6 distinct seats: 6! = 720.

text: The value of 0! is:
explanation: By convention/definition, 0! = 1.

text: The number of ways to choose 3 students out of 10 for a committee (order doesn't matter) is:
explanation: This is a combination (order irrelevant): C(10,3) = 120.

text: The number of permutations of the letters of the word 'APPLE' is:
explanation: APPLE has 5 letters with 'P' repeated twice: 5!/2! = 60.

text: How many diagonals does a hexagon (6 sides) have?
explanation: Total line segments between 6 vertices = C(6,2) = 15; subtract the 6 sides to leave only diagonals = 9.

text: The number of ways to arrange the letters of 'MISSISSIPPI' is given by 11!/(4!4!2!) because:
options: There are only 4 distinct letters total
M appears once, I appears 4 times, S appears 4 times, P appears 2 times
explanation: MISSISSIPPI has 11 letters: M×1, I×4, S×4, P×2 — dividing by the factorial of each repeat count removes overcounting of identical-letter swaps.

explanation: (x+1)² = x²+2x+1, standard binomial square expansion.

explanation: Setting a=b=1 in (a+b)ⁿ gives the sum of all coefficients = 2ⁿ.

explanation: By the AM-GM inequality, the arithmetic mean of two distinct positive numbers always exceeds their geometric mean.

text: Two lines with slopes m1 and m2 are perpendicular if:
explanation: The standard perpendicularity condition for two lines is that the product of their slopes equals −1.

The general form of a linear equation Ax + By + C = 0 represents:
explanation: A first-degree equation in x and y (linear, no squared terms) always represents a straight line.

text: The equation x² + y² = 25 represents a circle with radius:
explanation: Comparing to x²+y²=r², r²=25, so r=5.

text: The circle with centre (h,k) and radius r has the equation:
explanation: This is the standard centre-radius form of a circle's equation.

text: In the parabola y² = 4ax (a>0), the axis of the parabola is:
explanation: For y²=4ax, the parabola opens along the x-axis (symmetric about the x-axis), which is its axis.

text: For the parabola y² = 12x, the value of 4a (comparing to y²=4ax) is:
explanation: Direct comparison: 4a=12.

text: For the parabola y²=12x, the focus is at:
explanation: 4a=12 so a=3; for y²=4ax the focus is at (a,0) = (3,0).

text: In an ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with a>b, the eccentricity e is given by:
explanation: This is the standard eccentricity formula for an ellipse with major axis along x.

text: A conic section with eccentricity e=1 is a:
explanation: By definition, e=0 is a circle, 0<e<1 ellipse, e=1 parabola, e>1 hyperbola.

text: The eccentricity of a hyperbola is always:
explanation: Hyperbolas are defined by eccentricity strictly greater than 1.

text: In 3D space, a point is represented by:
explanation: A point in 3D (Cartesian) space needs 3 coordinates: x, y and z.

The three coordinate planes in 3D divide space into how many octants?
explanation: Just as the x-y axes split a plane into 4 quadrants, the three mutually perpendicular coordinate planes split 3D space into 8 octants.

text: The coordinates of the midpoint of the segment joining (1,2,3) and (3,4,5) are:
explanation: Midpoint = average of each coordinate: ((1+3)/2,(2+4)/2,(3+5)/2) = (2,3,4).

text: A point lying on the y-axis has coordinates of the form:
explanation: Points on the y-axis have both their x and z coordinates equal to zero.

text: lim(x→2) (x²−4)/(x−2) equals:
explanation: Factor: (x²−4)/(x−2) = (x−2)(x+2)/(x−2) = x+2 for x≠2; taking the limit as x→2 gives 2+2=4.

text: The derivative of xⁿ with respect to x is:
explanation: This is the standard power rule for differentiation.

text: The derivative of a constant c is:
explanation: A constant function has zero rate of change everywhere, so its derivative is 0.

text: The derivative of sin(x) is:
explanation: This is a standard derivative result: d/dx(sin x) = cos x.

text: The derivative of x³ at x=2 is:
explanation: d/dx(x³) = 3x²; at x=2, this is 3×4 = 12.

text: lim(x→0) sin(x)/x equals:
explanation: This is the standard fundamental trigonometric limit, equal to 1.

text: The product rule for derivatives states d/dx[f(x)g(x)] equals:
explanation: The product rule: derivative of a product is first-times-derivative-of-second plus second-times-derivative-of-first.

text: For the data 6,7,10,12,13,4,8,12 the mean is:
Mean deviation about the mean is always calculated using which values of the deviations?
explanation: Mean deviation uses the absolute value of each deviation from the mean/median, so that positive and negative deviations don't cancel out.

text: Variance is defined as the:
options: Square root of the mean deviation
explanation: Variance = (1/n)Σ(xi−x̄)², the average of the squared deviations from the mean.

text: Standard deviation is:
explanation: By definition, SD = √variance.

text: If all observations in a data set are increased by a constant k, the variance:
explanation: Adding a constant shifts every value but doesn't change the spread of the data, so variance is unaffected (only the mean shifts by k).

text: The coefficient of variation is defined as:
explanation: CV = (standard deviation / mean) × 100, used to compare relative variability across data sets.

text: When a fair coin is tossed once, the probability of getting a head is:
explanation: A fair coin has 2 equally likely outcomes; P(head)=1/2.

text: When a fair die is rolled, the probability of getting an even number is:
explanation: Even numbers on a die: 2,4,6 — 3 out of 6 equally likely outcomes, so P=3/6=1/2.

text: The probability of an impossible event is:
explanation: By definition, an event that cannot occur has probability 0.

text: The probability of a sure (certain) event is:
explanation: A certain event always happens, so its probability is 1.

text: If P(A) = 0.3, then P(not A) equals:
For two mutually exclusive events A and B, P(A∪B) equals:
explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot both occur (P(A∩B)=0), so the addition rule simplifies to P(A)+P(B).

text: In drawing a single card from a well-shuffled deck of 52, the probability of drawing a king is:
explanation: There are 4 kings out of 52 cards: 4/52 simplifies to 1/13 — both describe the same probability.

text: Two dice are thrown. The probability of getting a sum of 7 is:
explanation: There are 6 ways to get sum 7 out of 36 total outcomes: (1,6)(2,5)(3,4)(4,3)(5,2)(6,1) → 6/36 = 1/6.
